messages.subject: Datalab workshop NEXT WEEK
messages.body_plain:
D-RUGgies,
Datalab is offering a four-day workshop next week to teach folks how to use R, Git/Github, and the command line in your research. It's free to register so join us! Details are below.
-W

Introduction to Collaborative and Reproducible Research Practices with R (9/12-15)

This four-day in person workshop series (9/12, 9/13, 9/14, 9/15) at UC Davis DataLab <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/> provides an introduction to coding, with an emphasis on leveraging open source tools to develop workflows for collaborative and reproducible research. The goal of this series is to increase research integrity via exposure to basic command line tools and version control (Git), collaborative cloud tools (GitHub), programming (R), and data and software management best practices. Materials build across the sessions and attendance at all is required. All UC Davis graduate students and postdocs with little to no prior programming experience are eligible to apply. Upon successful completion of the series and additional assessments, UC Davis graduate students and postdocs are eligible to claim 3 badges through the Research Computing <https://gradpathways.ucdavis.edu/research-computing-pathway> GradPathways credential program.

Space is limited so register now! <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/introduction-to-collaborative-and-reproducible-research-practices-with-r-part-1-of-4/>

Stay Connected

Want to receive our newsletter and information about other upcoming workshops, jobs and grants, and other opportunities? Sign up for our mailing list! <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/mailing-list/> And check out our Research and Learning Clusters <https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/research-and-learning-clusters/>, including the Davis R Users Group, Python Users Group, our new Julia Users Group, and more!

Questions? Email datalab-...@ucdavis.edu.

messages.subject_clean: Davis R Users Group Fall 2022 announcement
messages.body_plain:
Greetings D-RUGgies!

The Davis R Users' Group is returning from summer hiatus and resuming our regular meetings Wednesdays 10am-noon in the Datalab classroom on the third floor of Shields Library (room 360!) Meetings resume the first Wednesday of the Fall quarter (Sept. 21) with a short presentation from yor coordinators followed by a work group for the remainder of the time.

A D-RUG work group is an unstructured time to ask and answer questions from the community, or simply work in company with other R enthusiasts. You can join by Zoom, as well.

D-RUG maintains a Discourse site where you can post questions for the D-RUG community and get answers outside of the regular Wednesday meetings. We recommend posting your questions there even if you are coming on Wednesday, because the questions and answers represent a knowledge base that folks can refer back to in the future.

The discourse site is d-rug.discourse.io <http://d-rug.discourse.io>. Details for joining the Wednesday meetings via Zoom will be sent out with the weekly announcements. We look forward to seeing you in the new quarter!

Finally, the Datalab is hosting a four-day workshop for members of the UC Davis community who want to get up to speed on R and/or to other tools like shell scripting, Git, and Github. That workshop will be held NEXT WEEK, Sept. 12 to Sept 15 (Mon-Thurs). Details and a link to register are at:
https://datalab.ucdavis.edu/eventscalendar/introduction-to-collaborative-and-reproducible-research-practices-with-r-part-1-of-4/

Best,
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.body_plain:
Happy Week 2!

This is your weekly reminder of tomorrow's R Users Group work group. As usual, we'll be meeting from 10-noon on Wednesdays. We will be meeting in a hybrid format, via zoom <https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/92807937862>, and in the Data Lab classroom (360 Shields Library). If you're attending virtually, please post your questions to the discourse site ahead of time. Info + links below.

Best,
Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

________________________________________________________________
Please remember to post your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

For those not familiar with D-RUG, the R Users' Group is a weekly working group to get some help with R-specific coding problems. The coordinators are various and sundry coding connoisseurs, ranging from UCD data scientists to grad students on campus. We meet for 2 hours in an open-forum format, so you can treat D-RUG as a communal, co-working environment: come hang out and chat, work on your own, seek help, make friends. Or, a little bit of everything! Check out our website <https://d-rug.github.io/> for more information.

We are also seeking presenters! It is nice to mix things up with occasional presentations. In the past, we've had (15- to 45-minute) presentations ranging from data types, to tidyverse tools, to spatial data, to the Google Earth Engine plugin for R. If you would like to hone your teaching, need an excuse to perfect your cRaft, or want to show off a cool R trick you learned, shoot us an email and we can add your presentation to our calendar (see below)! Presentations can be in-person or virtual (and in-person presentations will be streamed for virtual attendees).

Current presentation schedule:

Oct 5: Creating a package (Liza)
